Stacking trains a second-level model on predictions from several base learners. Training it on in-sample predictions lets it exploit overfitting patterns unavailable at deployment. Generate each training row's base predictions from models fitted without that row, using group/time-aware folds when needed. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/ensemble.html)

Fit the meta-model on those out-of-fold features, then refit base models on allowed training data for serving. In-sample stacking does not literally always assign 100% weight to one model; the real issue is biased meta-training information. Keep preprocessing within folds and reserve an independent evaluation set for the entire stacked pipeline.
